page.overview:
What is Ocarina of Time?

N64 release|jp= November 21, 1998|uk= December 11, 1998|au= December 18, 1998}} GCN release iQue Player release Wii VC release

Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack release

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the fifth main installment of and the first to be released for the Nintendo 64. It was one of the most highly anticipated games of its age, and is listed among the greatest video games ever created by numerous websites and magazines. It was released in Japan on November 21, 1998, the United States on November 23, 1998, Europe on December 11, 1998, & Australia on December 18, 1998. It is the first game in the long-running franchise to display 3D graphics.

Widely considered to be a masterpiece, it most famously scored the first perfect 40/40 score in Famitsu Magazine - a feat that only 26 games (including , and ) have ever achieved. In addition, G4 television declared it "the #1 game of all time" as well as Nintendo Power. is listed in Guinness World Records - Gamer's Edition 2008, as the highest ranked game of all time. In the 2010 Gamer's Edition, was updated as "the most critically acclaimed game of all time." It is also the highest scoring game of all time on Metacritic, at 99/100. It has also been ranked the greatest video game of all time by dozens of other publications. Therefore, like its contemporary Super Mario 64, Ocarina of Time is universally considered one of the most important and influential games of not only the Zelda franchise but the video game industry as a whole, and is essentially a repeat of The Legend of Zelda in terms of revolution for the action-adventure genre but in 3D. With 7.6 million copies sold worldwide, for 19 years, this installment was the best-selling standalone title of the series until Breath of the Wild in 2017 - itself selling a whopping 35.3 million (primarily due to being a launch title for the Nintendo Switch).

Also known as: Ocarina.
